speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Michael, Kobbie Mainoo said afterwards that  he loves playing for you. The players want  
to fight for you, they want to die for you. It  is a bit extreme, but it shows what they think  
of you. However you want to dress it up, you  have delivered sides that have beaten Man City  
and Arsenal and Chelsea, and now Liverpool.  What do you think about doing this job for  
Manchester United? Because I think everyone  thinks this should now be your job. Yeah,  
maybe. I think that is one of the biggest things  for me, trying to get the best out of people,  
helping players and giving them the opportunity  to go and perform and do what they are good at,  
really. There is that side, and then there is  obviously being part of it today and seeing  
this place alive and bouncing at the end. It is  a real joy and a pleasure to be in the position.  
I think as a group of players, they need a lot of  credit for the run, putting that together, and the  
coaching staff as well, especially for the amount  of work that goes on. I am sat here answering  
questions, but there is a lot of good work that  goes on beyond me. The pleasing thing about the  
spirit and the togetherness of the group, to see  that camaraderie and looking after each other,  
it was tested obviously at 2-2, and seeing them  really sticking in and fighting for each other,  
that is what we want. We want a team to be proud  of and the boys have certainly given us that. And  
what is it about this team, or this performance,  that impresses you that maybe people do not always  
see and appreciate? There was a lot today to be  happy with really and, like you said, to be proud  
of. I think we thought, players available wise,  that they would try and overload the midfield  
and it was going to be a big challenge for us to  try to close the space through the middle of the  
pitch. We have got some really dangerous forwards,  but we are asking them to do a lot of work without  
the ball as well, and that is part of being a good  team. The way we closed that space and made it  
difficult for them, they have got some fantastic  players and they made it difficult for us,  
but I thought the way we stuck at that especially  pleased me a lot, I have to say. The way the  
supporters got behind us after the two goals, it  is easy after that point to get frustrated, to go  
the other way a little bit, and I thought, again,  spirit and character shows when it is a little bit  
of a challenging time. So I think to feel that we  have built that, and we are in a position where  
we will all stick together, has really pleased  me a lot. And it was just two mistakes. Amad and  
Senne have both been immense for us and offered  so much within the group and the team, and to put  
us in this position. So that, building on to the  end of the game, in the way that we stuck at it,  
bounced back, finished well, players coming off  the bench and making a difference, I thought  
it is probably that spirit and togetherness for  everybody that satisfies me the most with that.  
Hi, Michael. You mentioned a lot there about what  you have built in that spirit and togetherness,  
and getting the fans onside over the last four  months. Ten wins in 14 games. Do you feel like  
you have earned the right to build on that and  take that into next season? Because, I mean,  
it has been perfect, really, what you have got  over the last four months. It has been a good run,  
I think. We have obviously beaten some very, very  good teams and it has been challenging. Sometimes  
we have won it in some ways, sometimes we have got  to win it in other ways. But, yeah, listen, I love  
doing what I am doing. It is a great position for  me to be in and it feels pretty natural, if I am  
totally honest with that. I am not being blasé,  because it is a difficult role, but it feels that  
I have been here a long time in different times,  on and off. I kind of understand what it brings  
and to be sat in this position is a good position  to be. Just following on from that, Mike, will you  
be disappointed now if you do not get this job?  We will have to wait and see. All we can do,  
I think when we came in, Champions League, to be  honest, was a little bit in the distance and we  
wanted to try and get back into Europe. So to be  where we are, what the players have put together,  
with three games to spare, is a good achievement.  I see it as just being a step, though. We are  
not over-celebrating it, but whatever is going to  happen is going to happen. I can always do my best  
work for the club and for the players especially,  and try and help them as best as we can and then  
see what happens after that. I know you said a  couple of times you do not want to over-celebrate  
qualifying for the Champions League. Just in  practical terms, when you are looking at making  
that next step, does it make that easier? I do not  know, maybe you have got more money to spend in  
the summer, maybe you can attract better players.  Is that how you are looking at it? No, definitely.  
It is a huge step, do not get me wrong, for  so many reasons. On the playing side, it is a  
big step. The sense that there are signs  of improvement and being in a position now,  
like I say, where we are with three games to go,  there is a lot of satisfaction that comes with  
that. But that cannot be everything. That is  kind of the point I am making. I think there  
is a lot of credit deserved to the staff and  the players for doing that, but we want more  
of that. We expect more of that consistently and  that is the message really, of let us try and push  
on and keep improving. It is not just to sit back  and think, no, that was all right, that was good,  
we have achieved. Mike, you spoke about  togetherness. The players clearly are quite a  
tight-knit group. How have you managed to develop  that? Or is it something that was sort of there  
before but needed a bit more extra attention?  Yeah, I can only say from what I have faced  
and seen from my own eyes really, and ever since  we came back through the doors, I think the boys  
have responded really well to it. I think it comes  through trust as well, how you treat each other,  
the trust between us and the belief certainly that  I have got in them and the staff have got in them.  
We spoke about that before the game, about how  much belief we have got in them. So trying to  
give them that confidence. They are really good  players and it can be a really good team when we  
put things in place, and that has proved to be the  case over recent months. Hi, Michael. I know it is  
a delicate matter, but I am sure it is in the news  about Sir Alex. Is there any comment that you have  
on behalf of the club? I have not got any updates.  I do not know the latest as we stand now. I did  
hear about it before the game, so I was aware  of it before the game. All I can say is I wish  
him well. I was very affected by it, the news,  and we just hope he is all right. I just do not  
know the latest, but we hope for him to be in good  shape and we wish him all the best. I am certainly  
thinking of him and hopefully the result, when  he hears about it, gives him a good boost.  
If you are still around next season or not, I  suppose one issue is the squad. Because Newcastle  
this season struggled with Champions League  football and Premier League football. Your squad  
is kind of a small one. Is that something you can  press on the club, regardless of what happens,  
that the squad needs bulking up? Because you need  quality as well as support. That is obviously  
the next challenge, of being in a position  where there are more games. It has been a bit  
frustrating at certain points because we have had  big gaps between games. There is a positive and a  
negative to that, but certainly the balance  of the squad, what it looks like, strength,  
depth, that is part of the conversations. Like I  said when I came in, I was not ever going to make  
decisions just to get to the end of the season. It  was always for the benefit of the whole football  
club moving forward. So we are definitely well  aware of what that should and could look like,  
and where we want to try and get to. Hi,  Michael. On Bruno and his performance today,  
I know you said all that you can say about  him in the past few weeks, but he came close  
to getting that assist record. I am just curious  about the reasoning behind the sub at the end,  
because it is pretty rare to see him come off  the board, to be honest. It was just there was  
a minute or so to go and we thought we would get  Lenny on the pitch. Obviously Josh had come on,  
Pat came on, Amad had come on as well, and there  was nothing behind that. Thanks, everyone. Cheers.
title: Michael Carrick post-match press conference | Manchester United 3-2 Liverpool | Premier League
